node_definition.done_when: The staleness reading reuses recovery's _worker_launched_after_manifest rather than composing a second one. A new tests/test_a_stale_manifest_does_not_license_promotion.py builds a resumed run with a live worker pid and a complete manifest written before that attempt's launch, and crew complete refuses it. The same run with its manifest written after the launch promotes. The named negative control (restore the terminal-manifest-only admission) makes the refusal case promote. In the same file, _unreviewed_refusal no longer says a run is classified running because no review is stored: it states the classification, and separately that no review is stored. Before editing, the worker measures which tests pass at base only because a stale manifest is admitted, by closing the gate in a scratch copy, and records their ids. Any such test outside this fence is not edited: the manifest reads blocked and names each id for a scope widening. The gate is every test file that imports reckon.crew.promotion, plus tests/test_ledger.py and tests/test_a_live_worker_still_owes_its_review.py, run with -n 8 at base and at head. Both suite arms are recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Every log's first line names its revision, and its last line is a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/a-stale-manifest-does-not-license-promotion.html records the change. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: _require_worker_stopped_before_promotion in reckon/crew/promotion.py refuses a run whose terminal manifest predates the live attempt's launch, so a run resumed mid-turn cannot promote the previous attempt's record (followup f-crpc-a-stale-manifest-does-not-license-promotion).
